prompt: How many servers does one MCP client talk to?

choices.text: Exactly one
choices.why: Right. A host with two servers has two clients.

choices.text: As many as the host connects
choices.why: That is the host; each client has one server.

choices.text: One per tool the servers offer, so a server with three tools gets three clients
choices.why: Clients are per server, not per tool.

choices.text: None; the server talks to the model
choices.why: The server never sees the model.

prompt: Which design principle of the specification does this lesson test?

choices.text: That servers should be written in Python, so that every host can import them
choices.why: Servers can be written in any language; the protocol is the contract.

choices.text: That every tool call needs a person's approval
choices.why: Approval is the host's decision, not a principle of the protocol.

choices.text: That a server sees neither the conversation nor other servers
choices.why: Right. The history stays with the host.

choices.text: That servers must run remotely
choices.why: Servers can be local processes or remote services.

prompt: With the Claude host, what was the probe server's parent process?

choices.text: hosts.py itself
choices.why: That was the case for the OpenAI and Google hosts.

choices.text: labllm, which starts servers on request
choices.why: labllm never starts servers; it is the model provider.

choices.text: The init process, as for a system service
choices.why: It was a child of the host's process tree.

choices.text: The Claude Code CLI
choices.why: Right. The MCP client lives in the CLI subprocess of lesson 9.

prompt: Why does the lesson print environment variable names and never values?

choices.text: Values are always empty in a stdio server
choices.why: They are not; the keys had values.

choices.text: Because names are shorter
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

choices.text: Because the operating system hides values from child processes
choices.why: A child process reads its own environment's values freely.

choices.text: Showing a key is the leak being taught
choices.why: Right. The point is that the server was able to read them, not what they are.

prompt: Why is the Google host's behaviour the most dangerous of the three?

choices.text: Because it crashed the run
choices.why: The run finished normally.

choices.text: Because it sent the conversation to both servers
choices.why: Each server got only its calls.
